Having a journal of any sort is very personal. I have made my journal public here first and foremost, because I do not trust myself to keep an accurate record privately of my learning. Secondly I want to climb to the top of the RTM ladder!

I envision that I will update this first post to form a table of contents, an organised linked record as opposed to a linear read through. I am imagining coming back to visit regularly over the 12 months time to see a post littered with links to nuggets of discoveries I have made and documented in this journal.

Let's begin.

H1/H4 - I noticed GJ had been compressing to a marked Support line now Resistance. M5 - I drop down as low as M5 to find price structure at this previous support line to find the pocket of potential supply. An FTR was found. Caution - Price has already visited this area. An FTB has been and gone. Trading to the right - Asian session sent price towards the FTR with a strong bullish candle. But price stalls, price consolidates and does not break higher. London Open is also unable to break higher, PA on the M30 chart I had been observing creates long upper wicks two times. I send my sell order to my broker.

Thank you benhur.

Continuation: M5 - Price declines sharply, engulfing the lower time-frame support and forming a new FTR immediately after with momentum. Caution - Price bounces noticeably forming a V shape on this timeframe. I am always cautious about this type of approach. Trading to the right - Caution noted, price hasn't created new demand, nor is price reacting of 'fresh' demand on the HTFs I observe. Price actually stalls before the FTR and begins to curl over. I place a limit order to provide best value. I am filled and watch the HTF Price Action to justify holding the trade.

Thanks strudl.

Conclusion: TG1 & TG2 reached. Hindsight: This trade very quickly showed I could have doubled the trade reward by waiting longer. I can think of various tasks for my to-do list. This could be the catalyst to collect statistics on taking different type of trade exits. There is always a decision to be made at each stage of the trade. Entries. Active trade period. News events. Exits. Perhaps in this case I could have employed a trailing stop. Or waited for PA in the opposite direction. Sorry guys just thinking out loud here. Expectation vs Anticipation vs Doubt vs Cold Hard Statistics! <--- This is what I want to build. Sometimes I feel you can spend so much time trying to find that perfect entry and when you finally get it, it doesn't end there, your guard is a little down, and then you realise the tough battle to fight when it comes to exits. Maybe a little more. Maybe a little less.

H4 - I watched price find support @ 1.47. A bullish outside bar into a supply zone (marked with red line). Price did not progress higher in the Asian session. Caution - AU news to be wary of. Possible change in sentiment given the Price Action of a the bullish H4 candle at a reasonable spot on the chart for support to form. Trading to the right - My bias is short. The weekly chart tells me down. The daily chart tells me down. It is only a matter of safe stop placement. I execute a sell order prior to news, knowing that AUD headfakes are usually quite reliable to place stops behind recent supply/demand zones. Thinking ahead - There are some weekly targets a couple of hundred pips lower that I have my eyes on. I will watch price on the H4 and up charts for other exit opportunities.

WK/M30 - Price arrives at prior weekly resistance area. Let's assume there are willing buyers here. Once the S/R is hit we watch for price structure to confirm our bias. M30 shows that we have an engulf of the most recent FL. A good sign of things to come to put the odds in our favour. Caution - AU news to be wary of. Trading to the right - Bias is long based on proximity of weekly resistance, anticipating to become temporary support. What actually happened - As you can see I took the trade before news. Price action confirms this bias ahead of time. Stop was however placed safely below the LTF FTR. It is actually the 2nd time back as the news spike collects remaining buy orders.

Hatching plans on USDCHF. This was just triggered as I am typing this post.

M30 - Price is at Daily supply. Creating my short bias. An engulf of minor support levels. Diamond like pattern forming. Caution - Price hasn't engulfed the FTR currently holding price UP and news has used this FTR a third time to fill more buy orders. Approach to supply not pretty. My bias could be ill informed or a fakeout play still possible. Trading to the right - Trading the FTB to this FTR for science. Learn by doing.

Read The Market -Momentum is bearish as evidenced by the long bear candle to the left of the M30 chart. This creates the bias to find supply. -The FTR I have chosen held the most significance to my eyes. It aligned well with LTF FTR and price structure. -Asian session created the FTR but it was choppy coming out; London ran with it to create new lows in recent days. If you think you feel ready to learn QMs, I would recommend you focus on finding QM's that happen on LTF. There are LOTS of them. The best QM's to learn from will be very obvious and have a form of symmetry about them. Please re-read the article and observe these things about QM price: 1. The location at which the pattern occurs 2. The symmetry of the pattern 3. The momentum of each engulf 4. The approach 5. The reaction 6. What causes the low to form, what causes the high to form, what causes the lower low to form, what causes the higher high to form? (and visa versa for the opposite setup) 7. How far does price go as a result of the setup?

After you do this, find in historical charts price patterns that look almost exactly like the examples. There's more than meets the eye.

What I think you really should do very thoroughly FIRST is to make sure you've done all your homework. Get comfortable identifying supply and demand, support, resistance, rbd, dbr, ftr, fl, dbd, rbr. Know all that stuff like the back of your hand.

While you're feeling confident you are now an expert at marking up your chart with supply/demand etc., be sure to look up the definition of the word engulf. Think about what it means in regards to trading. Dream about it daily! I do. Why does price engulf anything? What does that actually mean? Apply it to MULTIPLE time frames. One engulf may not be greater than the other. I want you to keep coming back to this forum for advice but please make sure you do the homework. Practice makes perfect. Good luck friend.

Hello SyT.

Firstly, good job on running through the various scenarios you could be making, but you're still wondering which scenario you choose will lead to profit? What I think you really should be asking is how do you know what trading decisions to make as well as the when and the why? A lot of this will come down to how disciplined and concious you are with your decision making and knowing (having the PROOF) if those decisions are profitable for you over a large sample size (You've forward tested the sh*t out of your decision making, you have tried various scenarios of the same trades and compared the results).

At the end of the day you will have to make one decision over another (trade or no trade, limit order or wait n see etc.) and what might be 'right' one day will be 'wrong' the next but one of your key objectives in trading should be to minimize risk so you've got the 'wrong' decisions covered that way at least! Remember.. you simply cannot 'WIN' every single trade regardless of how well prepared you were for all possible scenarios.

OK OK ok so I have rambled and I haven't told you anything you don't already know...guess what I probably can't actually help you for this one trade nor decide for you the most effective approach in the future. But here's the part where I make some suggestions anyway. Treat trading like a business right? This is one way to address the dilemma...gather PROOF that one decision is better than the other.

If you want to put in the real hard work, FORWARD test 100 trades similar to your USDCAD analysis and compare the stats (equity curve, expectancy etc.): 1. In the 1st account place the limit order, with SL and TP and leave it be. 2. In the 2nd account place a limit order...AFTER the REACTION validates the zone, with SL behind reaction pattern and TP with consideration to price structure of the APPROACH. 3. In the 3rd account duplicate scenario 1. but apply some trade management using the HTF. i.e. trail the stop, what is the reaction, how does this effect the outcome of my SL and TP placement, how is price behaving as it comes close to your sl or tp 4. In the 4th account duplicate scenario 2. but apply some trade management using the HTF. i.e. trail the stop, how does this effect the outcome of my SL and TP placement, how is price behaving as it comes close to your sl or tp 5. In the 5th account duplicate scenario 2 but instead use a market order where you can comfortably define your risk and reward 6. ADD all the scenarios you're interested in understanding how it effects your longer term performance

...I think you get the picture..You're testing combinations of decisions and seeing which ones are the most effective and which ones are useless!

By doing this, not only will you learn a thing or two about reading the market but you have now collected high quality reliable EVIDENCE, reflective of YOUR decision making and you will know where YOUR strengths and weaknesses are in regards to applying each scenario and you will know which scenarios you will want to continue forward with. Essentially, you're evolving your own trading decision tree/process map/flow chart. You're eliminating unreliable trading decisions and focusing your future attention on improving profitable decisions. Rinse and repeat. Eventually you will be 5 years deep in your career and all that hard work and the knowledge you have gained about your trading decisions will be called 'experience', and you will instinctively know what decisions to make and when.

Trading is a lot of hard work. Let's revisit your USDCAD dilemma, assuming it aligns with all the RTM teachings... except of course for the fact that you're committing to a trade decision before you've even witnessed the approach or the reaction. Maybe you just leave the limit order with SL & TP, maybe you are right and it's a perfect trade, but ask yourself, what does that really mean in the grand scheme of things, do I rule out all the other scenarios because this one time this strategy worked? Of course not, you want the BEST trade execution & trade management strategies that work for you, the only way to find that out is to measure them against each other, and choose what works for you.

p.s. I personally wouldn't have a limit order here anyway, because as you have established it has indeed invalidated the original analysis and price is now coming FROM a place of evident demand and the supply to stop its run is yet to be determined (this could be a rule in your trading plan like 'too much uncertainty for a limit order'). I would instead have an alert 10 pips before the zone, and be interested in watching the APPROACH and the REACTION as it happens. This usually provides a lower risk entry anyway or perhaps keeps you out of the trade altogether. So in response to your last question, no I would delete the order and get excited about watching the right of the chart unfold.

Many times, it's just a case of marking the best levels above/below price for each chart. setting alerts, and then just waiting for price to reach them. The main benefit to trading this many instruments is that you can trade only the more significant levels without too much waiting in between. You can then even start exploring why Diamonds begin to occur, how is that a HHH or LLL will occur, what are the factors that contribute to that extra push?

So what are the key attributes for a sell QM? 1. Left shoulder (a high) 2. New demand (low) 3. The head (higher-high) 4. An engulf of the new demand (lower-low) - for higher probability you want a good surge in price, a break with a bit of conviction! 5. A retracement of price to around the left shoulder or nice supply structure around the area (anticipating a lower-high)

Once you understand the key framework and can apply it to the chart you can begin to fine tune the trade by combining the zone with confluencing factors and other recognisable patterns on LTFs such as FLs or DBDs.

So in the best interest of actually getting a handle of this beautiful pattern and remaining in the present, please do the following for me (just for now): ignore the left of the chart, ignore the bigger picture and simply work to observe a decent quantity of them. At this stage of your learning. I recommend you forget about looking for them on the daily charts and get down on the M1/M5 charts and start mapping them out, they happen fast and they happen frequently (at least once or twice a session on each pair). Once you get the hang of retrospectively identifying them, demo trade the darn things real time! There is no substitute for first hand experience of anticipation. Don't spend too much time backtesting historical data. Forward test your ability to recognise the pattern in real time, you will only ever learn what to do through stepping yourself through the process over and over again. Wait for the left shoulder, wait for the higher high, wait for the engulf, place a limit order for the right shoulder, place your stop beyond the head, and target an obvious fresh zone. Forget about R:R at this stage. Trade management and fine tuning will come with time.
